description: Visual editor for TechDocs (MkDocs) pages, with the same Markdown fidelity as the Backstage plugin
config.openVisualByDefault: Open pages of a MkDocs `docs_dir` in the visual editor instead of the Markdown text. Use **Reopen Editor With…** to switch to the text.
config.images.maxSizeMB: Largest image, in MB, that the visual editor saves to the `assets` folder of the docs. Images go into the repository: large files weigh on every clone and on publishing.
config.local.publishPanel: Show the **Publishing** panel in the Explorer: save a draft to a branch, open a pull request, follow the checks and send it, without leaving VS Code. Needs a clone with a GitHub remote.
config.github.scopes: Scopes requested when signing in to GitHub. Use `public_repo` for public repositories only.
config.branchPattern: Name of the branch created for a draft when you are on the default branch. `{login}` is your GitHub login and `{path}` the page path.
config.drafts.skipCi: **Save draft** adds `[skip ci]` to the commit message, so the pipeline only runs on **Save and check**.
config.verification.mode: Where the checks come from. The repository `.techdocs-editor.yaml` wins over this setting.
config.verification.mode.auto: The pipeline when the repository has one (workflows or required checks), otherwise the formatting check of the editor
config.verification.mode.pipeline: Always wait for the checks of the pipeline
config.verification.mode.editor: Only the formatting check of the editor
config.verification.startTimeoutSeconds: Seconds to wait for the first check before warning that nothing started.
config.verification.checkHelp: Plain-language message shown when a check fails, by check name. Example: `{ "Links": "A link points to a page that does not exist." }`
config.polling.intervalSeconds: Seconds between check queries while something is running. Nothing is queried while the window is in the background.
config.polling.idleIntervalSeconds: Seconds between queries when nothing is running.
command.checkDocs: Check the documentation of the repository
command.prepareDocs: Prepare the documentation in this repository
config.templates.paths: More folders with templates, relative to the workspace folder: page templates (`.md` files with a `template:` block) and site templates (subfolders with a `template.yml`). They come after `.techdocs/templates/` of the site and of the workspace, which are always read.
config.templates.repository: Company-wide templates from a GitHub repository: `owner/repo`, optionally with a folder and a branch or tag (`acme/docs-templates/templates@v3`), and the host for GitHub Enterprise (`ghe.acme.com/acme/docs-templates`). Same format as `.techdocs/templates/`. They come after the repository's templates and before the built-in ones. Read when the template list opens, at most once an hour, and kept for offline use. In an untrusted workspace, only the user setting counts.
config.templates.builtIn: Show the templates that come with the extension. Turn off to offer only the repository templates.

viewsWelcome.check:
Check what TechDocs needs to build your documentation: mkdocs.yml, the nav, catalog-info.yaml, links and images.
[Check the documentation](command:techdocsEditor.checkDocs)
config.catalog: How the check treats `catalog-info.yaml`. The `catalog` key in the repository's `.techdocs-editor.yaml` wins over this setting.
config.catalog.auto: Check the TechDocs annotation if the file exists; without it, only a hint.
config.catalog.required: Backstage reads the catalog-info.yaml of the repository: a missing file is a problem, with a fix that creates it.
config.catalog.off: Backstage registers the docs some other way: nothing about catalog-info.yaml.
walkthrough.title: Get started with TechDocs Editor
walkthrough.description: Write TechDocs pages in a visual editor, from templates, and check them before publishing.
walkthrough.site.title: Open or create a documentation site
walkthrough.site.description:
The extension works on MkDocs sites: a mkdocs.yml with a docs folder. No site yet? Prepare the documentation: it starts from a template and uses what the repository already has, such as the README or a docs folder.
[Prepare the documentation](command:techdocsEditor.prepareDocs)
Or start from scratch with a site template.
[New documentation site](command:techdocsEditor.newSite)
walkthrough.sidebar.title: The TechDocs sidebar
walkthrough.sidebar.description:
Pages in the order of the site menu, what to fix before publishing, and the optional publishing panel, all in one place.
[Open the TechDocs sidebar](command:workbench.view.extension.techdocs)
walkthrough.page.title: Start a page from a template
walkthrough.page.description:
Runbook, ADR, tutorial, postmortem and more, with the sections each kind of page needs. The page goes into the nav and opens with the first text to replace selected.
[New page from template](command:techdocsEditor.newPage)
walkthrough.visual.title: Edit like a document
walkthrough.visual.description:
The visual editor saves plain Markdown, with formatting problems shown in plain language. Pages open as text by default.
[Open pages in the visual editor by default](command:workbench.action.openSettings?%5B%22techdocsEditor.openVisualByDefault%22%5D)
walkthrough.check.title: Check before publishing
walkthrough.check.description:
What TechDocs needs and is missing or wrong, with a fix you see as a diff before applying.
[Check the documentation](command:techdocsEditor.checkDocs)
walkthrough.publish.title: Publish without Git commands (optional)
walkthrough.publish.description:
For people who would rather not deal with branches: draft, check and send for review from a panel.
[Turn on the publishing panel](command:workbench.action.openSettings?%5B%22techdocsEditor.local.publishPanel%22%5D)
walkthrough.company.title: Company templates (platform teams)
walkthrough.company.description:
Keep your templates in one GitHub repository and point every docs repository to it.
[Set the templates repository](command:workbench.action.openSettings?%5B%22techdocsEditor.templates.repository%22%5D)
config.mode: Where documentation from a GitHub repository opens (the **Open documentation from GitHub…** command and `vscode://edtroleis.techdocs-editor/open` links).
config.mode.auto: From GitHub, or the local copy when the repository is in the workspace (you choose)
config.mode.local: Only the local copy in the workspace
config.mode.remote: Always from GitHub, even when the repository is in the workspace
config.github.host: GitHub server of your company (GitHub Enterprise Server), for example `github.example.com`. Links and the **Open documentation from GitHub…** command accept it besides `github.com`.
config.sites: Documentation sites offered in the TechDocs view and checked in **Maintenance**: folders of a `mkdocs.yml` (or a folder above them), relative to the workspace. Empty: all of them. Use **Choose which sites appear…** in the view.
viewsWelcome.chooseSite:
Choose the documentation you want to edit.
[Choose documentation…](command:techdocsEditor.chooseSite)

config.maintainer: Show the **Maintenance** section in the TechDocs sidebar: checking the documentation (mkdocs.yml, nav, catalog-info.yaml, links and images), preparing the repository and its options. For whoever maintains the documentation; people who only write pages do not need it.
